summary: Snapshot 2026-10-10. The Irkutsk story has moved into a new phase. On Oct 8, Rospotrebnadzor (Russia's public health agency) said medical observation of all contacts had ended, and it called reports of a second case false. The Irkutsk governor then lifted the quarantine, as Reuters, The Star and Kyiv Independent reported on Oct 8–9. According to the same reports, Russian authorities say about 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens. Russian authorities told WHO that no plague case has been recorded. WHO says it still does not know how she was infected, and Tedros said WHO cannot fully assess the risk without more information. Mainstream coverage (NBC, NPR, NYT, BBC, CNN, FT, AP, Axios) has moved from 'what is plague' to three things: how plague is diagnosed and why the cause can stay unknown, international reporting rules (IHR), and 'don't panic' explainers. Topic search is near its peak. The best openings now: (1) a dated status Short, as the breaking-news rule asks; (2) new 'why' angles that few creators cover yet: 'pneumonia of unknown origin', and why the 1–4 day incubation explains why observation ended after about a week; (3) evergreen search questions that keep pulling traffic after the news fades (person-to-person spread, symptoms, curable, US cases, pets). Bioweapon, cover-up and family-claim angles are rejected. Re-check every status line at publish time and copy CDC's US wording exactly ('an average of five', range 0–17, at the 10-09 check).

candidates.topic: Plague case in Russia: what's confirmed vs suspected as of Oct 9, 2026. Russian authorities lifted the quarantine and ended contact observation, while WHO says it still can't fully assess the situation
candidates.angle: A dated status decoder with every line credited. Rospotrebnadzor (Oct 8): observation of contacts ended, and reports of a second case are 'false'. The Irkutsk governor lifted the quarantine. Russian authorities told WHO no plague case has been recorded. WHO: cause of the pneumonia still unknown, and it cannot fully assess the risk. Make clear that 'not confirmed' is not the same as 'ruled out'. Put the newest development in the first beat. Use for the first plague long-form and a breaking-news Short.
candidates.why_now: The status changed on Oct 8–9: quarantine lifted, contact observation ended, second-case reports denied. Our playbook's breaking-news rule calls for an unscheduled 'status as of [date]' Short, and status explainers had the strongest pull at this stage.

candidates.topic: Why observation of pneumonic plague contacts can end after about a week: the 1–4 day incubation (CDC) explained
candidates.angle: The quarantine just ended, and people are asking why that matters. Pneumonic plague symptoms usually appear within 1–4 days of exposure (CDC). That is why health authorities watch contacts for a set period and may give preventive antibiotics. We explain the logic without claiming it proves what caused her illness. Not confirmed is not the same as ruled out. Add the urgent-care line.

Plain language, calm tone, no cover-up framing.

candidates.topic: Plague vs COVID: how each spreads, incubation and treatment, and why experts say a global outbreak is unlikely
candidates.angle: Name both sides. COVID is a virus that spreads through the air, and people can spread it before symptoms. Pneumonic plague is a bacterium that spreads through close-contact droplets, mostly from people who are already very sick, and antibiotics treat it. Cite BBC and expert explainers, and credit each claim to the source that made it. No 'next pandemic' framing.

candidates.topic: Is there a plague vaccine? Gavi's answer: vaccines have existed for 100+ years, but none are widely available, and new ones are in development
candidates.angle: Search-question Short built on Gavi's Oct 8 explainer. Killed vaccines offered limited protection against pneumonic plague. Live (weakened) vaccines are used in some countries, but reliable effectiveness estimates are lacking. WHO lists better vaccines as a priority. Keep every claim scoped to the vaccine type the source describes (avoid the S3 10-08 scope error). Russian officials said the worker had been vaccinated: if mentioned, attribute it and don't draw conclusions.
